title: Source Authority Ladder
summary: Choose evidence by ownership, directness, currency, scope, and independence instead of treating every search result as equally trustworthy.
prerequisites: A bounded research question and an as-of date

sections.title: Rank authority for the specific claim
paragraphs: Start with the organization that owns the fact: a product behavior belongs to current provider documentation, a standard to its issuing body, a law or regulation to the responsible government source, and a measured result to the underlying data and method. Use reputable analysis to interpret primary material, discover disagreement, or add context—not to replace a more direct source.

Authority is claim-specific. A vendor is authoritative about its documented interface, but not automatically about comparative quality. A source can be credible yet stale, outside the relevant region or version, based on a different population, or too indirect to support the sentence you want to write.

sections.title: Record a source decision
paragraphs: Do not paste restricted documents or personal data into an unapproved AI product. Record a safe label and retrieve protected evidence through an authorized workflow.

code.label: Source authority card

Source type: [PRIMARY | SECONDARY | AGGREGATOR]

Verified on: [YYYY-MM-DD]
Independence: [INTEREST OR CONFLICT TO CONSIDER]
Decision: [USE | CORROBORATE | BACKGROUND | REJECT]
Reason: [WHY THIS SOURCE FITS THIS CLAIM]

sections.title: Expected evidence and verification
paragraphs: The expected evidence is a traceable source set in which every material claim has at least one source that directly supports it, volatile claims use current owner documentation, and important uncertainty or disagreement remains visible.

Open every cited source, locate the supporting passage, confirm version and date, and test whether the sentence says more than the source. For consequential or contested claims, seek independent corroboration and document why sources disagree before drawing a conclusion.
sections.callout: Search ranking, confident prose, and citation count do not establish authority.

sections.title: Worked case: two claims, two best kinds of evidence
paragraphs: Use the following synthetic packet. Every item is invented for practice and is not evidence about a real provider, product, benchmark, or result. The research question is: As of 2026-06-30, what can we responsibly say about the fictional Orion API version 2.4? Claim A asks whether the documented interface accepts a field named temperature. Claim B asks whether Orion is more accurate than Nova on the fictional CedarQA evaluation.

The best evidence differs. For Claim A, the owner’s dated version-specific interface documentation is the most direct source. For Claim B, the vendor is not automatically authoritative because comparative quality is a measured claim. Prefer an independently reproducible measurement with a disclosed method, dataset, version, and results. A vendor statement can describe what the vendor claims, but cannot by itself establish comparative quality.

Do not turn the dimensions into a universal numerical score. Consider ownership, directness, currency, scope, independence, provenance, and corroboration together. A source may be strong on one dimension and weak on another.

Source type and independence are separate. PRIMARY means the source is original evidence or an issuer’s own statement for the claim. SECONDARY means it reports, analyzes, or reproduces evidence created elsewhere. An external report containing the authors’ own original measurement is PRIMARY for that measurement, even if it is independent of the vendors. Independence describes interests and provenance; it does not determine source type and neither independence nor primary status guarantees truth.

sections.title: Worked source cards and dispositions
paragraphs: A source card records a decision for one material claim, not a general reputation score for the source. The cards below deliberately show different decisions for different claims. USE means the source is suitable support for the narrowly stated claim. CORROBORATE means it is useful but should not stand alone. BACKGROUND means it supplies context without directly establishing the claim. REJECT means it should not support the claim as written.
The date 2026-06-30 is the as-of date in this exercise. A date in a card is not proof that a source is still current after that date.

Primary and secondary describe the source’s relationship to the evidence. Independence is a separate question about interests and provenance. S4 is PRIMARY because the lab reports its own measurement, while it is also independent of the vendors. That makes it appropriate for the bounded measured result, not automatically true or universally generalizable.

sections.title: Resolve the disagreement without hiding uncertainty
paragraphs: S5 says Orion is the most accurate, while S4 reports Orion at 71/100 and Nova at 76/100 on a named evaluation. S6 appears to agree with S5, but its provenance says the wording was copied from S5, so it adds no independent evidence. S8 reports Nova’s 76% under Nova’s own protocol, but the packet does not show that its protocol matches S4. The disagreement is therefore partly about result and partly about method.

The bounded conclusion is: S1 supports the statement that Orion API 2.4 documents temperature as a numeric parameter from 0 through 2, with default 1. S4 supports the narrower statement that, in the reported CedarQA v1 evaluation, Orion 2.4 scored 71/100 and Nova 3.1 scored 76/100 under the described method. The packet does not establish that either model is universally more accurate, that S4 and S8 are directly comparable, or that S5’s broad marketing claim is true.

Missing information includes S4’s full released artifacts and whether its scoring script was independently rerun, S8’s complete protocol and item-level results, the provenance of S7, confidence or uncertainty information for the 100-item comparison, and whether any provider or lab changed the models after the stated evaluation dates. The responsible next step is to retrieve and compare methods, versions, prompts, scoring rules, and raw or reproducible artifacts through an authorized workflow.
sections.callout: A disagreement is not resolved by choosing the source with the strongest tone. First identify whether the sources address the same claim, scope, version, population, metric, and method.

sections.title: Copyable worksheet
paragraphs: Copy the packet and fill one card for each material claim. Use one claim per card. For provenance, write relationships such as copied-from, cites, derived-from, or independently-reproduces. Mark UNKNOWN rather than guessing. A source’s publication date, verification date, and product version are separate fields.

Your final statements must distinguish directly stated facts from inferences. Include at least one corrected statement, one source you reject or limit, one provenance relationship, and one uncertainty caused by missing information.

sections.title: Independent task: changed inputs
paragraphs: Do this task before reading the answer key. The changed question is: As of 2026-07-10, can you state that the fictional hosted service Atlas accepts a max_tokens field, and can you state that Atlas is faster than Borealis on the fictional RiverBench test? The source packet below is synthetic and does not describe real services or measurements.

Produce at least four source cards: one for the interface claim, one for the comparative-speed claim, one for a tempting but limited source, and one for an inaccessible or provenance-uncertain source. Build two provenance relationships. Write a corrected pair of statements and identify at least two UNKNOWN items. Do not infer current behavior from a stale version, and do not infer comparative quality or speed from a vendor’s product announcement.

Pass criteria: 1) the interface decision uses the dated Atlas owner document for Atlas 5.0; 2) the speed decision uses the independent RiverBench measurement only for its stated versions, hardware, workload, and method; 3) a copied mirror is not counted as independent; 4) the answer names a real disagreement or limitation; 5) every conclusion is bounded by scope; 6) cards contain all template fields.
For T3, classify the source as PRIMARY for the authors’ own measurement, not SECONDARY. It is independent of Atlas and Borealis, but source type and independence are separate fields.

sections.title: Hints for the changed-input task
paragraphs: Hint 1: Split the question into two claims. The organization that owns an interface is different from the organization or method that can support a comparative latency result.
Hint 2: For the interface, compare T1 and T2 by version and date. For latency, look for a named workload, hardware, sample, metric, and reproducible method.

Hint 3: T5 is a mirror of T3, so it may help locate T3 but does not add independent corroboration. T4 has an interested owner and no inspectable measurement. T6 cannot be evaluated until authorized access supplies its contents and provenance.
Hint 4: A safe conclusion can say what happened in a named test. It should not say that one service is universally fastest unless the evidence supports that broader scope.

sections.title: Answer key and mistake-specific feedback
paragraphs: A strong answer makes the following bounded decisions. T1 is USE for the claim that Atlas hosted API 5.0 documents max_tokens as an integer from 1 through 4096. T2 is CORROBORATE or BACKGROUND because it documents Atlas 4.1 and is stale for Atlas 5.0. T3 is USE for the bounded RiverBench result. T4 is REJECT for a comparative latency claim. T5 is CORROBORATE at most as a locator for T3, never independent evidence. T6 is BACKGROUND or REJECT until it is accessible and its identity, method, and scope can be checked.

The corrected statements are: Atlas’s version 5.0 schema directly states that the completion request accepts max_tokens from 1 through 4096. In the reported RiverBench workload on the stated hardware, Atlas 5.0 had a median end-to-end latency of 820 ms and Borealis 2.2 had 760 ms, so Atlas was slower in that test. It remains UNKNOWN whether the result generalizes to other workloads, hardware, traffic levels, or service regions.

Mistake-specific feedback: If you use T2 for Atlas 5.0, you ignored version scope. If you use T4 as proof that Atlas is fastest, you treated marketing as measurement. If you count T5 and T3 as two independent reports, you missed provenance. If you use T6’s alleged result, you treated inaccessible evidence as verified. If you reverse the speed conclusion, check the arithmetic and units: 820 ms is greater than 760 ms, so Atlas has higher median latency in the stated test. If you claim universal speed, you expanded a bounded result beyond its population and method.

T3 is PRIMARY for the authors’ own measurement even though it is independent of the compared vendors. PRIMARY versus SECONDARY describes the relationship to the evidence, while independence describes interests and provenance. Neither label guarantees truth.

sections.title: Optional offline exercise: validate card structure
paragraphs: This offline exercise validates packet shape, required nonempty string fields, and controlled vocabulary labels. It does not determine whether a claim is true, whether a URL resolves, whether a source is authoritative or independent, or whether a decision is justified. All records are synthetic. The checker reports structural observations only and never assigns source authority automatically.

Save the single code object below as `validate_cards.py`, then run `python3 validate_cards.py`. It uses only Python's standard-library `json` module, documented at https://docs.python.org/3/library/json.html. The program includes assertions for a structurally valid original-measurement PRIMARY card, the six-card worked fixture, explicitly recorded unknowns, a blank required field, an invalid source type, a malformed row, list, object, and null enum values, malformed packet shapes, and invalid JSON. These assertions are tests, not claims that the program was executed while drafting this exercise.

Worked case: inspect `FIXTURE` and predict one diagnostic per card before running the program. Card 1 passes structural validation. Cards 2 through 6 respectively demonstrate a missing scope, an invalid decision, an invalid directness label, a row that is not an object, and a list-valued claim. A failure identifies the exact structural defect but does not prove that the underlying claim or source should be rejected.

Independent changed-input task: inspect `CHANGED_INPUT` without relying on the worked fixture and write the two expected card diagnostics. The answer key is printed under `CHANGED INPUT ANSWER KEY:` and reproduced in the expected-output section. Trace for card 1: every required field is a nonempty string, `UNKNOWN` is an explicitly allowed source type, and the other enum values are allowed, so it passes structure only. Trace for card 2: `owner` is blank and `BLOG` is not an allowed source type, so both defects are reported. The same validation method transfers to evidence about any provider because no provider name affects the rules.

sections.title: Expected output for the offline structural exercise
paragraphs: The text below is the independently specified expected standard output for `python3 validate_cards.py`. It is an answer key, not a claim that the program was executed during drafting. Python assertions are silent when they pass, so only the fixture diagnostics, changed-input key, and final self-test status appear.

The first six lines correspond in order to the six worked-case rows. Under the changed-input heading, the first card passes because its explicit `UNKNOWN` source type is allowed, while the second card reports both its blank owner and invalid source type. `SELF-TESTS: PASS` is printed only after every assertion has completed without raising an exception.

sections.title: Transfer the method across providers
paragraphs: The method is provider-neutral. For Meta or Llama, DeepSeek, Qwen, Mistral, Phi, NVIDIA, Z.ai, or any hosted service, first identify the exact claim and then find the owner of that fact. For an interface claim, inspect the current provider or project documentation for the exact product, model, API version, region, and date. For a comparative claim, seek an independent, reproducible measurement that names the models, dataset or workload, metric, hardware or environment, and method.

Do not assume that a provider’s documentation is authoritative about comparative quality, and do not assume that a hosted service behaves exactly like a downloadable model or a different deployment. Do not assert any current capability for Meta, Llama, DeepSeek, Qwen, Mistral, Phi, NVIDIA, Z.ai, or a hosted service without a dated source that directly supports the exact statement. A mirror of a provider page is provenance for discovery, not independent corroboration.
When access is restricted, record a safe internal ID and use an authorized retrieval workflow. Do not paste restricted documents or personal data into an unapproved AI product.
